newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds were off all day and ended somewhat lower on Thursday, but dealers said the undertone remained positive.

Market players did not notice any impact from the Dutch rise of the special advances to 3.00 percent from 2.90 percent in late afternoon. They said bonds could be boosted indirectly if the guilder regains strength versus the German mark as result of the rate hike, but the direct impact on the guilder was small.
The guilder was trading at 112.5825 per 100 marks after the rate hike versus 112.60 before the Dutch central bank raised the special advances.
One dealer said the Dutch central bank might decide to raise the special advances by another 10 basis points if the guilder remains weak versus the mark.
"The Dutch central bank could even decide to bring the Dutch special advances rate above the German repo rate," he said.
The German repo rate is comparible to the Dutch special advances and has been pegged at 3.00 percent for quite some time.
Dealers said investors were shortening their portfolio a little. Most business was done in the June 2002, November 2005 and the February 2007 bond.
